speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you're experiencing knee pain after increasing your physical activity; can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what it feels like, such as sharp, dull, or aching?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help me understand the severity, on a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate your pain, and does it radiate to your ankle or hip? Also, have you noticed any visible swelling, redness, or difficulty bearing weight on this leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

Given your description of pain over the medial tibia and recent increase in pivoting activities, I want to confirm if you feel tenderness directly along the medial tibial border and if you have any "giving way" sensation. REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_MRI
